legal.metaTitle: IT and AI for law firms in the Rio Grande Valley
legal.metaDescription: Bilingual intake that answers after hours, document handling that stays confidential, and IT built for a Valley law practice. Free assessment, one point of contact.
legal.heading: Technology for Valley law firms
legal.intro: A missed call is a missed case. Most people looking for a lawyer call three and retain whoever answers first, and in the Valley that call is as likely to be in Spanish as in English. The work below is about answering every one of them, and keeping what a client tells you confidential once you do.
legal.sofia: Sofía answers your line in the caller's language, takes the details of what happened, tells them what you charge for a consultation, and puts a real appointment on your calendar. She never gives legal advice and never says whether you will take the case. What lands on your desk is a formatted intake sheet, not a voicemail you have to call back to understand.

workflows.title: Intake that answers after hours
workflows.body: Calls at 8 PM and on Saturday get a real conversation instead of a machine. Details arrive in your inbox, structured the same way every time, before you open the office.

workflows.title: Conflict and confidentiality by design
workflows.body: Client information stays in accounts you own, with access limited to the people who need it. We work under an NDA whenever you want one, and we can tell you exactly where every file lives.

workflows.title: Document work that stops being retyping
workflows.body: Intake forms, engagement letters, and routine correspondence get filled from information you already collected, so the same client details are not typed four times.

faq.q: Will an AI give my callers legal advice?
faq.a: No. The assistant is built to collect facts and schedule, and is instructed to refuse anything that reads like advice or a prediction about a case. If a caller pushes, it says a lawyer will answer that and books the appointment.

faq.q: Is client information safe in an AI system?
faq.a: It is as safe as you set it up to be. We keep client data in accounts you own, restrict who and what can read it, and prefer tools that do not train on your content. We will put the specifics in writing before anything goes live.

faq.q: Can it handle Spanish-speaking callers properly?
faq.a: Yes, and that is the point. It answers in the language the caller uses, in the register a person actually speaks, not a translation of an English script.

medical.metaTitle: IT and AI for medical and dental practices in the Rio Grande Valley
medical.metaDescription: Bilingual scheduling, reminders that cut no-shows, and secure IT for a Valley clinic or dental office. Free assessment, one point of contact.
medical.heading: Technology for Valley clinics and dental offices
medical.intro: Your front desk is answering the phone, checking someone in, and handling a refill request at the same time. Most of what interrupts them is routine and repeatable, which is exactly the kind of work that can be handled before it reaches a person.
medical.sofia: Sofía answers in English or Spanish, books and reschedules appointments against your real calendar, and tells callers what they need to bring. She is built to stay away from anything clinical: no symptoms discussed, no advice given, and anything that sounds urgent is handed to a person immediately with the caller still on the line.

workflows.title: Scheduling and reminders in both languages
workflows.body: Appointments booked by phone at any hour, and reminders that reach patients the way they actually read messages. Fewer empty chairs, fewer callbacks.

workflows.title: Intake before the visit
workflows.body: Forms filled in advance, in the patient's language, so a visit starts with care rather than a clipboard.

workflows.title: IT that a regulated practice can defend
workflows.body: Access limited per person, devices managed and encrypted, backups that are tested rather than assumed, and a written record of how it all works.

faq.a: Compliance is a property of your whole practice, not of one tool, so nobody can honestly sell you it in a box. What we do is design the workflow to keep protected health information in systems you control, with access limits and an agreement in place with any vendor that touches it, and document it so your compliance advisor can review it.

faq.q: Will an AI talk to patients about symptoms?
faq.a: No. It schedules, confirms, and answers practical questions like hours and what to bring. Anything clinical or urgent goes to your staff right away, and the caller is told that is happening.

faq.q: We already have a practice management system. Does this replace it?
faq.a: No. It works around what you have. The assessment starts by looking at what you already pay for, because the cheapest improvement is usually a feature you own and are not using.

logistics.metaTitle: IT and AI for logistics and freight companies in the Rio Grande Valley
logistics.metaDescription: Dispatch that answers day and night, paperwork that fills itself, and IT built for cross-border freight. Free assessment, one point of contact.
logistics.heading: Technology for Valley freight and logistics
logistics.intro: Freight does not keep office hours, and the paperwork that moves with it is the same handful of fields typed over and over into different forms. Both are fixable without changing how you run loads.
logistics.sofia: Sofía answers the office line in either language, takes load and rate enquiries with the details you actually need, and books call-backs on your dispatchers' calendars. Drivers and brokers get a person's answer at 2 AM instead of a voicemail, and your dispatchers stop losing an hour a day to calls that were never urgent.

workflows.title: A line that is answered at 2 AM
workflows.body: Rate enquiries, check calls, and driver questions handled around the clock in English and Spanish, with anything genuinely urgent passed to a person.

workflows.title: Paperwork that fills itself
workflows.body: The same load details typed once instead of into four documents, with the routine parts of rate confirmations and status updates generated rather than retyped.

workflows.title: Systems that survive a bad day
workflows.body: Accounts, devices, and backups set up so that a lost laptop or a phishing email does not stop dispatch. Cross-border operations get the security review they rarely get.

faq.a: Only if you want it to and only inside rules you set. By default it collects the lane, the equipment, the dates, and the contact, then hands it to a person. Quoting is a business decision, not a technology one, and it should be yours.
No. It sits around whatever you already run and removes the typing and the phone traffic. We start by finding which repeated task costs you the most hours.

faq.q: Our brokers call at all hours from both sides of the border. Does that matter?
faq.a: That is the case this is built for. The line is answered in whichever language the caller opens with, and the message reaches your dispatcher in the form they need it.

trades.metaTitle: IT and AI for contractors and skilled trades in the Rio Grande Valley
trades.metaDescription: Answer every call from the ladder, quote faster, and get paid sooner. Bilingual systems for Valley contractors. Free assessment, one point of contact.
trades.heading: Technology for Valley contractors and trades
trades.intro: You cannot answer the phone from a roof, and the person calling you will call the next number on the list. Almost everything that costs a trades business money is the gap between a call coming in and someone getting back to it.
trades.sofia: Sofía picks up while you are on the job, in English or Spanish, gets the address and what is wrong, tells the caller your service call fee, and puts them on your schedule. You come down the ladder to a booked job instead of a voicemail, and you never lose a customer because you were working.

workflows.title: Every call answered, even from the ladder
workflows.body: A real conversation in either language while you are working, with the job details and the address in your hands by the time you check your phone.

workflows.title: Quotes and follow-up that actually go out
workflows.body: Estimates that reuse what you already collected, and follow-ups that happen on their own instead of when you remember on Sunday night.

workflows.title: A website that turns a search into a booking
workflows.body: Fast, bilingual, and built so someone who finds you on a phone can book or call in one tap. Your accounts and your domain stay in your name.

faq.q: I am a two-person shop. Is this overkill?
faq.a: It is aimed exactly at you. A large company has a receptionist; you have a phone in your pocket while you are working. The smaller the crew, the more a missed call costs.

faq.q: Will customers know it is not me?
faq.a: It introduces itself as your assistant. It does not pretend to be a person, and in practice callers mind far less than being sent to voicemail. It hands off to you whenever someone asks for it.

It depends on the volume of calls and what you want it to handle, and we scope it after a free assessment so you get a fixed number before anything starts. We will also say when the honest answer is that you do not need it yet.

agriculture.metaTitle: IT and AI for agriculture businesses in the Rio Grande Valley
agriculture.metaDescription: Connect field records, inventory, and invoicing, and answer the line in both languages. Practical technology for Valley growers and packers. Free assessment.
agriculture.heading: Technology for Valley growers and packers
agriculture.intro: Most Valley operations run on records that live in three places: a notebook, a spreadsheet, and somebody's memory. Season by season that works until the one week it does not, usually at invoicing or an audit.
agriculture.sofia: Sofía answers the office line in English or Spanish, takes buyer and supplier enquiries with the details you need, and books call-backs. During harvest, when the office is empty because everyone is in the field, the line still gets answered.

workflows.title: Records that connect to invoicing
workflows.body: What was picked, packed, and shipped tied to what gets billed, so the numbers reconcile without a week of chasing paper.

workflows.title: Reporting you can hand to a buyer
workflows.body: The traceability and volume reporting buyers increasingly ask for, produced from records you already keep rather than assembled by hand each time.

workflows.title: Systems built for how the work happens
workflows.body: Bilingual by default, usable on a phone in the field, and set up so a lost device or a failed drive does not take a season's records with it.

faq.q: Our records are on paper and in spreadsheets. Is that a problem?
faq.a: It is the normal starting point. The first step is usually connecting what you already keep rather than replacing it, because a system nobody in the field will use is worse than the notebook.

faq.q: Does the crew need to speak English to use it?
faq.a: No. Everything we build is bilingual from the start, not translated afterwards, because a tool people cannot read is a tool they will work around.

faq.q: Harvest is not the time to change systems. When should we start?
faq.a: The off-season, and the assessment is the right thing to do during the busy one. We look at where the season actually hurt and have the change ready before the next one.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.metaDescription: Answers about how Bespoke Intelligent Solutions helps Rio Grande Valley businesses with AI, IT security, and bilingual web design.
faq.intro: Straight answers about how we work, what we build, and how to get started.

whatIsBis.q: What does Bespoke Intelligent Solutions do?
whatIsBis.a: We're an IT and AI consultancy for Rio Grande Valley businesses. We help you adopt practical AI, modernize and secure your IT, and build fast bilingual websites — with one point of contact from strategy through delivery.

whoServe.a: Small and mid-sized Valley businesses — including legal, medical and dental, logistics and freight, skilled trades, and agriculture. Everything we do is fully bilingual in English and Spanish.

bespoke.q: What does “bespoke” mean for my business?
bespoke.a: It means we start with your workflow, your customers, and your two languages — not a template. We recommend only what earns its keep, and we build it to fit how you actually operate.

aiPractical.q: Is AI actually practical for a business my size?
aiPractical.a: Yes. We focus on removing real hours from your week — automating intake, scheduling, follow-ups, and document handling — not flashy demos. If a task is repeatable, there's usually a piece of it we can automate.

aiCost.q: How much does AI cost, and what's the return?
aiCost.a: It varies by scope, but we target automations that pay for themselves in saved time. The free assessment identifies the single automation with the fastest payback so you can start small and prove the value.

dataHandling.q: How do you handle our data and confidentiality?
dataHandling.a: We treat your data as confidential, work under an NDA when you want one, use least-privilege access, and prefer tools that keep your data in your own accounts. You own your systems and your data — always.

compliance.q: Do you work with regulated fields like legal and healthcare?
compliance.a: Yes. We're security-first and privacy-aware for fields like legal and medical/dental, and we design workflows with confidentiality and data protection in mind. We're not a substitute for your compliance counsel, but we build to support it.

ownWebsite.q: Do we own our website and accounts?
ownWebsite.a: Completely. Every build ships with the keys: your hosting, your domain, your accounts. No proprietary lock-in, no black boxes — clean code you can hand to anyone.

webWhat.q: What kind of web work do you do?
webWhat.a: Fast, modern, bilingual sites and web apps that convert — with native English/Spanish content, local SEO for the RGV, and analytics so you can see what's working.

howStart.a: Book a free, no-pitch assessment. We look at how your business runs today and show you the one improvement that pays for itself first. No obligation.

pricing.q: How do you price your work?
pricing.a: Most engagements are scoped to a fixed proposal after the free assessment, so you know the cost before we start. We right-size to your business rather than selling a one-size package.

remote.q: Do you work remotely or on-site?
remote.a: Both. We're based in Harlingen and serve the entire Valley, so we can work on-site when it helps and remotely when that's faster — whatever gets you results.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.metaDescription: How Bespoke Intelligent Solutions collects, uses, and protects your information.
privacy.intro: Bespoke Intelligent Solutions ("BIS", "we", "us") respects your privacy. This policy explains what we collect through this website, how we use it, and the choices you have. We keep it plain-language on purpose.
privacy.collectIntro: We only collect what we need to respond to you and run this site:
collectItems: Contact form: your name, business name, email, phone, industry, and message — so we can reply and prepare your free assessment.
Resource downloads: your name and email — so we can send you the resource and, if you opt in, occasional tips. The tips checkbox is off by default.
AI assistant: the messages you send our on-site chat assistant, so it can answer your questions.

Phone calls: when you call our business line, our AI receptionist keeps a written transcript and a summary of the call, the number you called from, and whatever you tell her — your name, what you need, and any appointment you book — so we can follow up. We do not keep audio recordings of calls.
Usage analytics: privacy-friendly, aggregate metrics about how our pages perform. This does not identify you.
privacy.useBody: We use your information to respond to inquiries, prepare and deliver assessments and resources, improve the site, and — only if you opt in — send occasional updates. We do not sell your information, and we never share it for advertising.
privacy.processorsIntro: We rely on a few trusted service providers to run the site. They only process your data to provide their service to us:
processorsItems: Resend — sends our transactional emails (download links and our notifications).
Neon / Vercel Postgres — securely stores resource-download sign-ups and leads captured by the chat assistant.
Vercel (Analytics & Speed Insights) — hosts the site and provides cookieless performance analytics.
BIS Platform (app.bis-rgv.com) — our own client platform, which hosts the contact form and the assessment scheduler and stores what you submit through them.
DeepSeek — provides the AI model behind our on-site chat assistant.
OpenAI — provides the realtime speech model behind Sofía, the AI receptionist who answers our phone line.
Telnyx — carries the calls to our business line.
privacy.cookiesBody: We use privacy-friendly, cookieless analytics. We do not use advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, so there is no cookie-consent banner to click through. Your browser may still use essential cookies needed for the site to function.
privacy.retentionHeading: How long we keep your data
privacy.retentionBody: We keep contact and resource submissions, and the transcripts and summaries of calls to our business line, only as long as needed to serve you and for our records, and we delete them when you ask us to or when they are no longer needed.
privacy.rightsBody: You can ask us for a copy of the information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it — at any time, no reason needed. Just email bespokeintelligentsolutions@gmail.com and we will take care of it.
privacy.childrenBody: This site is intended for businesses and is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect information from children.
privacy.changesBody: We may update this policy as our services change. When we do, we will update the date at the top of this page.
privacy.contactBody: If you have any questions about this policy or your information, email us at bespokeintelligentsolutions@gmail.com.

sofia.label: Bespoke Intelligent Solutions — our own front desk
sofia.title: Sofía, our AI receptionist
sofia.summary: Call our main line and Sofía answers. She is an AI — we would rather you read that here than wonder about it later. She handles the first conversation the way a good receptionist does: finds out what you need, answers what she can, and gets you on the calendar. This is not a demo sandbox. It is the same number printed at the top of this page.
facts: Answers our real, published business line — the number in our header and on our contact page, not a sandbox we reset between demos.
Speaks English and Spanish, and follows you if you switch languages in the middle of the call.
Books onto a real calendar. Ask for a free assessment and she checks live availability, places the appointment on our BIS Platform calendar, and you get a confirmation email like any other booking.

Leaves a durable record. Every call ends with a written transcript, a summary, and a lead in the same platform this website's contact form writes to — so nothing falls through between the call and the follow-up.
sofia.builtBody: A phone number routed over SIP into a realtime speech model, with the calendar, the lead database, and our email notifications wired in as tools the model can actually call — not a recorded menu tree. The website you are reading and the receptionist who answers the phone write to the same leads table: one pipeline, two front doors.
sofia.tryBody: Tap to call. Ask her what BIS does, switch to Spanish halfway through, or book a free assessment and watch it land in your inbox.
sofia.tryNote: Calls are transcribed and summarized so we can follow up properly.

harlingen.metaTitle: IT, AI & Web for Harlingen Businesses
harlingen.metaDescription: Bespoke Intelligent Solutions is based in Harlingen. Practical AI, IT security and bilingual web design for clinics, distributors and professional firms across the city.
harlingen.heading: IT and AI for Harlingen businesses
harlingen.intro: Harlingen is home. Our office is here, our number is a Harlingen number, and when a client wants somebody in the room it's a short drive rather than a flight. That changes what we can honestly promise about showing up.

sectors.title: Clinics and medical offices
sectors.body: Harlingen carries a serious share of the Valley's healthcare, and the pressure lands on the front desk: appointment calls, intake paperwork, reminders, and patients who would rather speak Spanish. Those are the first hours worth getting back, and they're usually handled by whoever happens to be closest to the phone.

sectors.title: Distribution and air freight
sectors.body: Valley International moves enough cargo to rank among the busier freight airports in the country, with wide-body freighters on the ramp. The businesses around it run on documents, tracking and dispatch — repetitive, deadline-bound work where a mistake costs a shipment. That combination is where automation actually pays.

sectors.title: Small professional firms
sectors.body: The offices where one person answers the phone, books the appointments, chases the invoices and updates the website. We're usually not replacing a system for them. We're replacing the fact that there isn't one.

harlingen.howBody: Being based here means we can start in person and stay reachable afterward. It also means we're accountable locally — this is where we live, and in a town this size a bad job follows you around.

mcallen.metaTitle: IT, AI & Web for McAllen Businesses
mcallen.metaDescription: Practical AI, IT security and bilingual web design for McAllen retailers, medical practices and multi-location businesses. Serving McAllen from Harlingen.
mcallen.heading: IT and AI for McAllen businesses
mcallen.intro: McAllen is the retail center for South Texas and northern Mexico, and about one in eight workers in the metro is in retail trade. That mix — high volume, thin margins, and a lot of walk-in and phone traffic in two languages — decides which problems are worth solving here.

sectors.title: Retail and multi-location businesses
sectors.body: When customers come from both sides of the river, your phone rings in two languages and your busiest hours are exactly the hours nobody can pick up. Something that answers in whichever language the caller uses, at the times you can't staff, isn't a novelty here — it's the baseline.

sectors.title: Medical practices
sectors.body: The McAllen–Edinburg medical corridor is one of the largest employers in the region. Practices carry the same front-desk load as anywhere else, plus the expectation of bilingual service, plus rules about how patient information is handled. We design for that last part first rather than last.

sectors.title: Cross-border operations
sectors.body: Businesses that quote, invoice or schedule across the border carry two sets of paperwork and two customer bases. Most of that work is structured and repetitive — the kind that survives on one person's memory and a spreadsheet until the week they take vacation.

mcallen.howBody: McAllen is about an hour from our office, so we work the way most clients there prefer: on site to understand the business and set things up, remote for the parts where driving would only slow it down.

brownsville.metaTitle: IT, AI & Web for Brownsville Businesses
brownsville.metaDescription: Practical AI, IT security and bilingual web design for Brownsville customs brokers, freight forwarders and port-adjacent businesses. Serving Brownsville from Harlingen.
brownsville.heading: IT and AI for Brownsville businesses
brownsville.intro: Brownsville runs on cross-border trade. It has the only deep-water seaport sitting directly on the U.S.–Mexico border, and the businesses around it — brokers, forwarders, carriers, industrial suppliers — live and die on paperwork moving on time.

sectors.title: Customs brokers and freight forwarders
sectors.body: Document-heavy, deadline-driven, and mostly the same work repeated with small variations: entries, quotes, status updates, the same five questions from every client every day. This is the clearest automation case in the Valley, because the work is high volume, structured, and expensive to get wrong.

sectors.title: Trucking and dispatch
sectors.body: Dispatch is a phone job and the phone doesn't stop. Where's my load, when does it clear, what does it cost. Those answers usually already exist in a system somebody has to stop and go look at — which is a good sign the answering can happen without pulling a dispatcher off the radio.

sectors.title: Port-adjacent industrial and services
sectors.body: The suppliers, yards and contractors around the port tend to have solid operations and thin IT. Often the right first project isn't artificial intelligence at all — it's making sure one ransomware email can't stop the loading dock.

brownsville.howBody: We serve Brownsville from Harlingen, close enough to be on site the same day when something matters. We work in English and Spanish because your customers, your drivers and your counterparts across the bridge do.

edinburg.metaTitle: IT, AI & Web for Edinburg Businesses
edinburg.metaDescription: Practical AI, IT security and bilingual web design for Edinburg law firms, healthcare practices and professional services. Serving Edinburg from Harlingen.
edinburg.heading: IT and AI for Edinburg businesses
edinburg.intro: Edinburg is the seat of Hidalgo County and home to UTRGV's main campus, which gives it an unusual mix for the Valley: courts and county offices, a large healthcare base, and a steady population of professional firms built around both.

sectors.title: Law firms and title offices
sectors.body: A county seat concentrates legal work, and legal work concentrates documents. Intake, conflict checks, deadlines, records requests, and clients who call to ask what's happening with their case. Legal is one of the five industries we build for, and confidentiality shapes the design instead of getting bolted on at the end.

sectors.title: Healthcare practices
sectors.body: Healthcare employs a share of Edinburg well above what a city its size would normally carry. Same front-desk pressure as everywhere, same bilingual expectation, same rules about patient information — and the same phone that turns into the bottleneck.

sectors.title: Professional and back-office services
sectors.body: Accounting, insurance, staffing — the offices that keep a county running. Work that arrives as forms and leaves as forms, where most of the labor is moving information between systems that were never introduced to each other.

edinburg.howBody: Edinburg is a straightforward drive from Harlingen. For firms handling confidential files we'd rather do the first session in person, look at the real workflow, and be specific about what leaves your building and what doesn't.

weslaco.metaTitle: IT, AI & Web for Weslaco Businesses
weslaco.metaDescription: Practical AI, IT security and bilingual web design for Weslaco growers, packing sheds and family businesses. Serving Weslaco from Harlingen.
weslaco.heading: IT and AI for Weslaco businesses
weslaco.intro: Weslaco sits at the center of Valley agriculture — Texas A&M has run an agricultural research and extension center here since 1923, and produce still sets the calendar for a lot of the businesses in town.

sectors.title: Growers and packing sheds
sectors.body: Agriculture is seasonal, and seasonal means the workload triples for a few weeks and the phone triples with it. Hiring for the peak is expensive; hiring after it starts is too late. Automating the repetitive part of the peak — orders, schedules, buyer questions, driver check-ins — usually costs less than either.

sectors.title: Agricultural services and equipment
sectors.body: The dealers, suppliers and service outfits around growing operations run on quotes, parts availability and service calls. When your customers are standing in a field, the ones who answer fastest tend to get the work.

sectors.title: Family businesses
sectors.body: A lot of Weslaco business is second and third generation, where the process lives in one person's head. Our first job is usually to write that down before automating anything — a process nobody can describe is a process nobody can hand over.

weslaco.howBody: We're across the mid-Valley regularly, and we plan around your season instead of ours. Nobody should be rolling out new software in the middle of harvest.

securityCheck.title: Free Website & Email Security Check
securityCheck.metaDescription: Check any Rio Grande Valley business website in about a minute. We read the same public records a browser and a mail server already see, and tell you in plain English what is exposed.
securityCheck.intro: Type your web address. In about a minute you will see whether someone can send email pretending to be you, whether your site is protected in the browser, and what to fix first. We only read public records — nothing is logged into, nothing is attacked.
securityCheck.allClearBody: The public checks all came back clean. A full review looks at things no outside scan can see: who has admin access, how backups are tested, what happens when someone leaves.
securityCheck.ctaHeading: Want the rest of the picture?
securityCheck.ctaBody: This check reads what is visible from outside. Most of what puts a Valley business at risk is not: shared passwords, no backups, one person holding every key. The assessment is free and takes 30 minutes.
securityCheck.disclaimer: This check reads public DNS records and the response headers your website already sends to every visitor. It does not log in, scan ports, or test any password.

errors.empty: Enter your web address to start.
errors.malformed: That does not look like a web address. Try it like yourbusiness.com.
errors.notPublic: That address is not a public website, so there is nothing we can check from out here.
errors.ipAddress: Enter a domain name rather than an IP address.
errors.unreachable: We could not reach that address. Check the spelling, or try again in a minute.
errors.rateLimited: That is a lot of checks in a short time. Give it a minute and try again.
errors.failed: Something went wrong on our end. Try again, or call us at (956) 506-1545.

https.title: Your site loads securely
https.pass: Your website answers over a secure connection.
https.fail: We could not load your site securely. Visitors may see a browser warning before they ever reach you.

httpsRedirect.title: Insecure visits are sent to the secure address
httpsRedirect.pass: Someone typing your address without “https” is moved to the secure version automatically.
httpsRedirect.fail: Someone typing your address without “https” stays on the insecure version, where anything they submit can be read in transit.
httpsRedirect.unknown: We could not tell. This is worth checking by hand.

hsts.title: Browsers are told to always use the secure address
hsts.pass: Once someone visits, their browser refuses to use the insecure version again.
hsts.warn: This is set, but it expires soon enough that most visitors will not benefit. A year or more is the norm.
hsts.fail: Not set. Every visit starts over on the insecure address before being redirected, which is the moment an attacker on shared Wi-Fi looks for.

csp.title: Only your own code can run on your pages
csp.pass: Your site tells browsers which code is allowed to run, which is what stops an injected script from reading your forms.
csp.warn: A policy exists but allows code from anywhere, so it stops very little.
csp.fail: No policy. If anything on your site is ever compromised, injected code runs with nothing standing in its way.

clickjacking.title: Your site cannot be framed inside another
clickjacking.pass: Nobody can load your site inside their own page and trick your customers into clicking something else.
clickjacking.fail: Anyone can load your site inside their own page. That is how a fake payment or login screen gets built on top of a real business.

nosniff.title: Uploads cannot be run as code
nosniff.pass: Browsers are told to treat your files as exactly what they are.
nosniff.fail: Missing. A file a customer uploads can be interpreted as code and run in another visitor's browser.

referrerPolicy.title: Your visitors' pages stay private
referrerPolicy.pass: Other sites are not told which of your pages a visitor came from.
referrerPolicy.warn: Not set, so every site a visitor clicks through to learns the exact page they left, including anything in the address.

cookieFlags.title: Cookies are protected
cookieFlags.pass: No cookies are set on your front page, or the ones that are cannot be read by scripts or sent insecurely.
cookieFlags.warn: At least one cookie can be read by scripts or sent over an insecure connection. If it is a login cookie, that is an account someone else can use.

serverDisclosure.title: Your software versions are not advertised
serverDisclosure.pass: Your site does not announce exactly which software and version it runs.
serverDisclosure.warn: Your site announces its exact software version, which tells an attacker which known exploit to try first.

spf.title: Only your mail servers can send as you
spf.pass: You publish a list of who may send email as your domain, and it tells receivers to reject everyone else.
spf.warn: You publish the list, but it asks receivers to merely flag impostors instead of rejecting them.
spf.fail: Anyone in the world can send email that looks like it came from your business. That is the single most common way a small business loses money to fraud.

dmarc.title: Impostor email is actually rejected
dmarc.pass: Mail that fails your checks is quarantined or rejected rather than delivered.
dmarc.warn: You have the record, but it is set to watch only, so forged mail is still delivered to your customers.
dmarc.fail: No policy, so mail servers have no instruction about what to do with email forged in your name, and most will deliver it.

mx.title: Your domain receives email
mx.pass: Mail servers are published for your domain.
mx.unknown: This domain does not receive email, so the email checks above matter less — though a domain that sends no mail should still say so.

certExpiry.title: Your certificate is not about to expire
certExpiry.pass: The certificate that proves your site is really yours has plenty of time left.
certExpiry.warn: It expires soon. Most providers renew automatically about a month out, so this close usually means a renewal is stuck.
certExpiry.fail: It expires within days, or already has. When it does, every visitor sees a full-page browser warning telling them your site is unsafe.
certExpiry.unknown: We could not read the certificate.

mixedContent.title: Your secure pages load only secure files
mixedContent.pass: Everything your page loads comes over a secure connection.
mixedContent.fail: Your secure page loads at least one file over an insecure connection. Browsers block or warn on these, which can silently break part of your site and undoes the padlock.
mixedContent.unknown: We could not read the page to check.

dkim.title: Your email is signed
dkim.pass: Your outgoing mail carries a signature that receiving servers can verify.
dkim.warn: We could not find a signing key under the selectors common providers use. If your mail is unsigned, more of it lands in spam and your DMARC policy has less to work with.
dkim.unknown: This domain does not receive email.

securityCheck.reportHeading: Want the full report by email?
securityCheck.reportBody: We will send everything above, with what each finding means and what to do about it, in one email you can forward to whoever looks after your systems.
securityCheck.reportSent: Sent. Check your inbox — and your spam folder, which is where a message about email security tends to land.
securityCheck.reportErrorInvalid: Check the email address and try again.
securityCheck.reportErrorRateLimited: That is a few reports in a short time. Try again in an hour, or call us at (956) 506-1545.
securityCheck.reportErrorFailed: We could not send that. Try again, or call us at (956) 506-1545.
securityCheck.reportPrivacy: We use it to send this report and to follow up once. No list, no sharing.

firstHourBack.title: Find your first hour back
firstHourBack.metaDescription: A two-minute estimate of how many hours a week a Rio Grande Valley business could hand back with a bilingual assistant and a couple of automations. Assumptions shown, nothing hidden.
firstHourBack.intro: Four questions about a normal week. You will get an estimate of the hours you could hand back, with every assumption behind it written out. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no email is required.
firstHourBack.callsLabel: Calls you miss in a normal week
firstHourBack.callsHelp: Calls that ring out, go to voicemail, or come in while you are on a job.
firstHourBack.adminLabel: Hours a week on repeatable paperwork
firstHourBack.adminHelp: Scheduling, intake, follow-up, retyping the same details into different forms.
firstHourBack.rateLabel: What an hour of your time is worth
firstHourBack.rateHelp: Optional. Leave it blank and we will not guess.
firstHourBack.spanishLabel: Share of your customers who prefer Spanish
firstHourBack.emptyBody: The estimate appears here as soon as you tell us about a normal week.

firstHourBack.hoursLine: About {hours} hours a week handed back
firstHourBack.hoursYear: {hoursYear} hours a year, at {weeks} working weeks.
firstHourBack.callsLine: About {calls} more calls a week answered

firstHourBack.valueBody: Your own hourly figure, multiplied by the hours above. It is an estimate, not a quote.
firstHourBack.bilingualBody: At that share of your customers, a bilingual front door is not a nicety. It is the difference between a caller staying on the line and calling the next business.

firstHourBack.assumption3: A working year is {weeks} weeks, not 52.
firstHourBack.assumption4: These are estimates for a conversation, not a quote. What your business would actually get back is what the free assessment is for.
firstHourBack.ctaHeading: Find out what the real number is
firstHourBack.ctaBody: Thirty minutes, no pitch. We look at how your week actually runs and tell you which single change pays for itself first — including when the honest answer is that you do not need us yet.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.metaDescription: How bis-rgv.com is built for accessibility, what we test, what we know is not perfect, and how to tell us when something does not work for you.
accessibility.intro: This site is built to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. That is the standard the Department of Justice set for state and local government websites, and it is the one we hold our own work to whether or not a client is required to.
accessibility.statusBody: Every page shape on this site is checked automatically against WCAG 2.1 A and AA rules on every change, in English and Spanish: the home page, service and industry pages, city pages, articles, the FAQ, both free tools, the contact page and the page a mistyped link lands on. As of the last check, all of them pass with no violations.
accessibility.honestHeading: What that does and does not mean
accessibility.honestBody: Automated testing catches roughly a third of real accessibility barriers. It can tell you a button has no name; it cannot tell you the name is confusing, or that a flow is exhausting to complete with a switch device. We have not commissioned an independent audit of this site or tested it with a panel of assistive technology users, and we will say so plainly rather than imply a level of assurance we have not bought.
accessibility.practice1: Keyboard first. Every control can be reached and operated without a mouse, and the focus ring is visible rather than removed for looks.
accessibility.practice2: Status is never colour alone. Where this site reports a result — a security finding, a form error — it carries an icon and a word as well as a colour.
accessibility.practice3: Motion respects the system setting. Everything that animates stops for a visitor who has asked their device to reduce motion.
accessibility.practice4: Both languages, natively. Pages declare their language so a screen reader pronounces them correctly, and Spanish is written rather than translated.
accessibility.practice5: Real text, real structure. Headings describe the page rather than style it, images that carry meaning are described, and decoration is hidden from assistive technology instead of read aloud.
accessibility.problemHeading: If something does not work for you
accessibility.problemBody: Tell us and we will fix it. Email or call, describe the page and what happened, and we will reply within two business days. If you need information from this site in another format in the meantime, ask and we will send it.
accessibility.helpHeading: If you need this for your own site
accessibility.helpBody: Cities, counties, school districts and special districts in Texas are covered by ADA Title II, which requires their websites and mobile apps to meet WCAG 2.1 Level AA. After the Department of Justice extended the deadlines in April 2026, public entities serving 50,000 or more people have until 26 April 2027, and smaller entities and special district governments until 26 April 2028. We remediate existing sites, test what you already have, and build new ones to the standard. Private businesses are not covered by Title II, and we still recommend the same standard, because the people it helps are your customers.
accessibility.updatedBody: Written {date}. It describes what is true of this site today, and we update it when that changes rather than leaving a date to age.

trust.title: How we protect your data
trust.metaDescription: The security questions a Rio Grande Valley business should ask a technology vendor, answered in advance: who can see your systems, where your data lives, what we do not claim, and what happens when the work ends.
trust.intro: Before a clinic, a law firm or a freight office lets anyone near its systems, someone has to answer a list of questions. This page answers them in advance so the conversation starts further along — and so you can see the answers before you ask.
trust.notBody: It is not an audit report. BIS has not been through SOC 2 and does not hold a security certification, and any vendor implying otherwise without showing you the report is selling you a feeling. What follows is how the work is actually done, stated plainly enough that you can hold us to it.
trust.accessBody: Access is requested per person and per system, for the work in front of us, and removed when that work ends. We do not ask for a shared login, and we do not need your passwords to do most of what we do — modern systems grant delegated access without handing over an account. Where a confidentiality agreement helps you sleep, we sign one before anything starts.
trust.ownershipHeading: Where your data lives, and who owns it
trust.ownershipBody: In accounts with your name on them. Your hosting, your domain, your database, your AI provider account. We prefer tools that keep your data in your own tenancy rather than pooling it in ours, and every build ships with the keys. If you replace us next year, nothing has to be extracted from anywhere — you already own it.
trust.vendorsHeading: Vendors that would touch your data
trust.vendorsIntro: Any service that would hold or process your data is named before it is used, not discovered later in a bill. These are the ones BIS builds on today:
vendorsItems: Vercel — hosts websites and applications we build.
Neon and Supabase — the databases behind those applications.
Resend — sends transactional email such as confirmations and notifications.
Telnyx — carries phone calls to an AI receptionist.
OpenAI — the speech model behind Sofía on a phone line.
DeepSeek — the model behind the assistant on this website. Client deployments use whichever provider the engagement calls for, and it is chosen with you rather than assumed.
Clerk — sign-in for the BIS Platform.
Upstash — rate limiting, which holds counters rather than content.
trust.vendorsOutro: If a project needs something not on this list, you hear about it before it is introduced.
trust.sofiaHeading: If we run an AI receptionist for you
trust.sofiaBody: Sofía keeps a written transcript and a summary of each call, the number it came from, and whatever the caller tells her. She does not keep audio recordings. Everything lands in your own account on the BIS Platform, where you can read it, export it, or delete it. Callers are told the call is handled by an assistant and that it is transcribed — being straight with the person on the line is not optional.
trust.regulatedHeading: Regulated work: legal, medical and dental
trust.regulatedBody: Compliance is a property of your whole practice, not of a product, so nobody can honestly hand it to you in a box. What we do is design the workflow so protected information stays in systems you control, with access limited per person, an agreement in place with any vendor that touches it, and the whole thing documented so your compliance counsel can review it rather than take our word for it. We are not a substitute for that counsel and will say so every time.
trust.siteIntro: The easiest vendor to check is the one in front of you, so here is what this site does and how to verify it yourself:
siteItems: A Content-Security-Policy that admits no third-party script origin, plus HSTS, clickjacking and MIME-sniffing protection on every response.
Invisible bot verification on the endpoints that cost money, with a per-address rate limit behind it.
SPF and DMARC published, so nobody can send email that appears to come from this domain.
No advertising or cross-site tracking cookies, and cookieless analytics — which is why there is no consent banner to click through.
Every page checked against WCAG 2.1 AA on every change.
Failures that lose an enquiry raise an alert to a person rather than a line in a log nobody reads.
trust.siteCta: Run our own checker against this domain
trust.incidentBody: Tell us and you will hear back from a person, not a ticket queue, within two business days. If a problem affects your data, you will be told what happened, what it touched and what we did about it — in that order, in plain language, without waiting for it to be tidy.
trust.exitBody: You keep everything: accounts, domains, code, data, and the documentation to run it. Access we were granted is handed back or removed. There is no proprietary layer to unpick and no fee to get your own systems back, because the arrangement never depended on you being stuck.
trust.updatedBody: Written {date}. It describes how BIS works today. When that changes, this page changes with it.
